definitions.english: Money is what we use to buy things. In Lesotho, we use Maloti and Lisente.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete ke seo re se sebedisang ho reka dintho. Lesotho re sebedisa Maloti le Lisente.

definitions.english: Money is special paper and coins that people use to pay for things.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete ke pampiri le ditjhepe tse kgethehileng tseo batho ba di sebedisang ho lefa.

definitions.english: Money helps us buy food, clothes, and other things we need.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete e re thusa ho reka dijo, diaparo le dintho tse ding tseo re di hlokang.

definitions.english: In Lesotho, our money is called the Loti.
definitions.sesotho: Lesotho, chelete ya rona e bitswa Loti.

definitions.english: Money is a tool for buying and selling things.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete ke sesebediswa sa ho reka le ho rekisa.

definitions.english: Money is a medium of exchange used to buy goods and services.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete ke mokgwa wa ho fapanyetsana o sebediswang ho reka thepa le ditshebeletso.

definitions.english: The Loti is divided into 100 Lisente.
definitions.sesotho: Loti e arotswe ka Lisente tse 100.

definitions.english: Money has three functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete e na le mesebetsi e meraro: ho fapanyetsana, ho metha boleng le ho boloka boleng.

definitions.english: The Loti is pegged to the South African Rand.
definitions.sesotho: Loti e hokahane le Rand ya Afrika Borwa.
Chelete e emela matla a ho reka.

definitions.english: Money serves as medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete e sebetsa e le mokgwa wa ho fapanyetsana, ho boloka boleng le ho metha boleng.

definitions.english: The Lesotho Loti (LSL) is pegged 1:1 to the Rand (ZAR).
definitions.sesotho: Loti ya Lesotho (LSL) e hokahane 1:1 le Rand (ZAR).

definitions.english: Money encompasses M0 through M3 with implications for liquidity.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete e kenyelletsa M0 ho ya M3 ka ditlamorao tsa liquidity.

definitions.english: Understanding money requires analyzing banking and monetary policy.
definitions.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa chelete ho hloka ho hlahloba dibanka le leano la lichelete.

definitions.english: Digital money represents a new form of financial inclusion.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete ya dijithale e emela mokgwa o motjha wa ho kenyelletsa batho ditabeng tsa lichelete.

examples.english: A bread costs M10. You give M10 and get bread.
examples.sesotho: Bohobe bo bitsa M10. O fana ka M10 mme o fumana bohobe.

examples.english: M1 is the same as 100 Lisente.
examples.sesotho: M1 e tshwana le Lisente tse 100.

examples.english: A sweet costs M5. A packet of chips costs M10.
examples.sesotho: Pompong e bitsa M5. Pakete ya chips e bitsa M10.

examples.english: M50 can buy five breads that cost M10 each.
examples.sesotho: M50 e ka reka mahobe a mahlano a bitsang M10 ka bonngwe.

examples.english: You have M20 and want to buy something that costs M15. You have M5 left.
examples.sesotho: O na le M20 mme o batla ho reka ntho e bitsang M15. O setse le M5.

examples.english: M50 can be exchanged for goods worth M50.
examples.sesotho: M50 e ka fapanyetswa ka thepa ya boleng ba M50.

examples.english: At 5 percent inflation, M100 today buys only M95 worth next year.
examples.sesotho: Ka inflation ya 5%, M100 kajeno e reka feela M95 selemong se tlang.

examples.english: M1 equals R1 because of the peg.
examples.sesotho: M1 e lekana le R1 ka lebaka la peg.

examples.english: Counting money: M20 + M10 + M5 = M35.
examples.sesotho: Ho bala chelete: M20 + M10 + M5 = M35.

examples.english: You receive M500 and can spend or save it.
examples.sesotho: O fumana M500 mme o ka e sebedisa kapa ho e boloka.

examples.english: The Loti-Rand peg means shared monetary policy with South Africa.
examples.sesotho: Peg ya Loti le Rand e bolela leano le kopaneng la lichelete le Afrika Borwa.

examples.english: M1,000 in cash has different implications than M1,000 in savings.
examples.sesotho: M1,000 ya cash e na le moelelo o fapaneng le M1,000 polokong.

examples.english: Depositing M500 enters the broader money supply.
examples.sesotho: Ho kenya M500 ho kena ka hara pokello e pharaletseng ya chelete.

examples.english: Purchasing power parity compares prices between Maseru and Bloemfontein.
examples.sesotho: Purchasing power parity e bapisa ditheko pakeng tsa Maseru le Bloemfontein.

examples.english: Mobile money like M-Pesa affects financial inclusion.
examples.sesotho: Mobile money e kang M-Pesa e ama ho kenyelletswa ditabeng tsa lichelete.

misconceptions.english: Money grows on trees — FALSE! People earn money by working.
misconceptions.sesotho: Chelete e mela difateng — HA SE NNETE! Batho ba fumana chelete ka ho sebetsa.

misconceptions.english: More money means more happiness — FALSE! Money helps but is not everything.
misconceptions.sesotho: Chelete e ngata e bolela thabo e ngata — HA SE NNETE! Chelete ea thusa empa ha se yohle.

misconceptions.english: Only adults use money — FALSE! Children can learn to use money too.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke batho ba baholo feela ba sebedisang chelete — HA SE NNETE! Bana le bona ba ka ithuta.

misconceptions.english: Debit cards are unlimited money — FALSE! They only access your account.
misconceptions.sesotho: Dikarete tsa debit ke chelete e sa feleng — HA SE NNETE! Di fihlella feela akhaonto ya hao.

misconceptions.english: The Loti and Rand are the same currency — FALSE! Different but pegged.
misconceptions.sesotho: Loti le Rand ke chelete e le nngwe — HA SE NNETE! Di fapane empa di hokahane.

misconceptions.english: Banks print money — FALSE! The Central Bank controls money supply.
misconceptions.sesotho: Dibanka di hatisa chelete — HA SE NNETE! Banka e Kgolo e laola tlhahiso ya chelete.

misconceptions.english: Cryptocurrency is legal tender in Lesotho — FALSE!
misconceptions.sesotho: Cryptocurrency ke chelete ya molao Lesotho — HA SE NNETE!

misconceptions.english: Money has intrinsic value — FALSE! Fiat money has value by decree.
misconceptions.sesotho: Chelete e na le boleng ba tlhaho — HA SE NNETE! Fiat money e na le boleng ka molao.

misconceptions.english: Inflation always hurts everyone — FALSE! Borrowers with fixed rates benefit.
misconceptions.sesotho: Inflation e utlwisa bohle bohloko — HA SE NNETE! Ba alimang ka fixed rates ba a rua molemo.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn how to count Maloti?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho ithuta ho bala Maloti?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to know where money comes from?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho tseba moo chelete e tswang teng?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about saving money?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka ho boloka chelete?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to understand what banks do with money?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho utlwisisa hore na dibanka di etsa eng ka chelete?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to learn about earning money?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o ka rata ho ithuta ka ho fumana chelete?

how_to.english: Count your coins and notes to know how much you have.
how_to.sesotho: Bala ditjhepe le dipampiri ho tseba hore na o na le bokae.
Ithute hore M1 e lekana le Lisente tse 100.

how_to.english: Practice buying small things to understand prices.
how_to.sesotho: Ikwetlise ho reka dintho tse nyane ho utlwisisa ditheko.

how_to.english: Understand that the Loti is pegged to the Rand.
how_to.sesotho: Utlwisisa hore Loti e hokahane le Rand.

how_to.english: Track how much money comes in and goes out.
how_to.sesotho: Latela chelete e kenang le e tswang.

how_to.english: Learn about inflation and purchasing power.
how_to.sesotho: Ithute ka inflation le matla a ho reka.

how_to.english: Understand monetary policy and the Common Monetary Area.
how_to.sesotho: Utlwisisa leano la lichelete le Common Monetary Area.

how_to.english: Analyze how digital money affects financial inclusion.
how_to.sesotho: Hlahloba kamoo chelete ya dijithale e amang ho kenyelletswa.

how_to.english: Study the money multiplier and fractional reserve banking.
how_to.sesotho: Ithute ka money multiplier le fractional reserve banking.

why.english: We need money to buy food, clothes, and other things.
why.sesotho: Re hloka chelete ho reka dijo, diaparo le dintho tse ding.
Chelete e re thusa ho rekisana ka toka.

why.english: Understanding money helps you make good choices.
why.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa chelete ho thusa ho etsa dikgetho tse ntle.
Chelete e etsa kgwebo e be bonolo.

why.english: Understanding money helps you manage finances.
why.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa chelete ho thusa ho laola lichelete.

why.english: The Loti-Rand peg stabilizes the economy.
why.sesotho: Peg ya Loti le Rand e tsitsisa moruo.

why.english: Money serves as store of value and unit of account.
why.sesotho: Chelete e boloka boleng le ho metha boleng.

why.english: Monetary policy affects inflation and growth.
why.sesotho: Leano la lichelete le ama inflation le kgolo.

why.english: Digital money is transforming financial services.
why.sesotho: Chelete ya dijithale e fetola ditshebeletso.

situation.english: You have M50. A bread costs M10. How many breads can you buy?
situation.sesotho: O na le M50. Bohobe bo bitsa M10. O ka reka mahobe a makae?

advice.english: M50 divided by M10 = 5 breads. You can buy 5 breads.
advice.sesotho: M50 arolwa ka M10 = mahobe a 5. O ka reka mahobe a 5.

lesson.english: Division helps you know how many things you can buy.
lesson.sesotho: Ho arola ho o thusa ho tseba hore na o ka reka dintho tse kae.

situation.english: A sweet costs M2. You have M10. How many sweets can you buy?
situation.sesotho: Pompong e bitsa M2. O na le M10. O ka reka dipompong tse kae?

advice.sesotho: M10 arolwa ka M2 = dipompong tse 5.

lesson.english: Understanding prices helps you spend wisely.
lesson.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa ditheko ho thusa ho sebedisa ka bohlale.

situation.english: You have M200. Transport costs M20 per day. How many days can you travel?
situation.sesotho: O na le M200. Dipalangwang di bitsa M20 ka letsatsi. O ka tsamaya matsatsi a makae?

advice.english: M200 divided by M20 = 10 days of transport.
advice.sesotho: M200 arolwa ka M20 = matsatsi a 10 a dipalangwang.

lesson.english: Budgeting daily expenses helps money last longer.
lesson.sesotho: Ho rera ditshenyehelo tsa letsatsi ho thusa chelete ho tshwarella.

situation.english: At 6% inflation, M1,000 today will be worth how much in buying power next year?
situation.sesotho: Ka inflation ya 6%, M1,000 kajeno e tla ba le matla a ho reka a bokae selemong se tlang?

advice.sesotho: M1,000 / 1.06 = M943 matla a ho reka.

lesson.english: Inflation erodes purchasing power over time.
lesson.sesotho: Inflation e fokotsa matla a ho reka ka nako.
